questions.title: Cheapest Cable Offer
questions.description:
Contractors submitted several cable offers for a fibre project, each quoting a price to link two poles. Before planning the network, the office just wants the single cheapest offer. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int cheapestOffer(int[][] edges)

Each row edges[i] = {u, v, w} describes one offer. It must return the smallest weight w among all offers.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v w" — an offer to link poles u and v at price w.

Output Format:
One line with the lowest quoted price.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 1 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V, 1 <= w <= 1000

questions.title: Zero In-Degree Count
questions.description:
Kahn's topological sort starts by spotting every node with no incoming edges — they are the tasks that can begin immediately. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int zeroInDegreeCount(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return how many nodes of the directed graph have in-degree 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a directed edge u -> v (0-indexed).

Output Format:
One line with the number of nodes that have no incoming edges.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Self-Loop Count
questions.description:
The tiniest possible cycle is a self-loop: an edge that leaves a node and lands right back on it. Counting them is a one-sweep scan. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int selfLoopCount(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return the number of nodes u that have a directed edge u -> u.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a directed edge u -> v (0-indexed).

Output Format:
One line with the number of self-loops.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Cheapest Incident Edge
questions.description:
Spanning-tree algorithms repeatedly ask: of all edges touching this node, which is the lightest? On a weighted adjacency matrix that is the smallest non-zero entry of the row. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int cheapestEdge(int[][] m, int u)

It must return the minimum non-zero weight in row u of the weighted adjacency matrix (0 means no edge). Row u is guaranteed to contain at least one non-zero entry.

Input Format:
Line 1: V. Then V lines, each with V space-separated weights — the symmetric adjacency matrix. Last line: the queried node u.

Output Format:
One line with the cheapest edge weight incident to u.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= weight <= 1000, 0 <= u < V

questions.title: Outgoing Weight Sum
questions.description:
Shortest-path algorithms relax outgoing edges one by one; a quick sanity drill is summing the travel costs that leave a node. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int outgoingWeightSum(int[][] m, int u)

It must return the sum of the non-zero entries in row u of the directed weighted adjacency matrix (0 means no edge).

Input Format:
Line 1: V. Then V lines, each with V space-separated weights. Last line: the queried node u.

Output Format:
One line with the sum of u's outgoing weights.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= weight <= 1000, 0 <= u < V

questions.title: Isolated Node Count
questions.description:
A node with degree 0 belongs to no connection at all — connectivity algorithms can skip it entirely when hunting components. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int isolatedNodes(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return how many nodes of the undirected graph have degree 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — an undirected edge.

Output Format:
One line with the number of isolated nodes.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Direct Connection Test
questions.description:
Before running any path search it is worth checking the trivial case: an edge that goes straight from s to t. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int hasDirectEdge(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int s, int t)

It must return 1 if the directed graph contains the edge s -> t, otherwise 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a directed edge u -> v. Last line: "s t" — the queried pair.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= s, t, u, v < V

questions.title: Course Prerequisite Count
questions.description:
A university catalog is a directed graph: an edge a -> b means course a must be completed before b. The direct prerequisites of a course are exactly its incoming edges. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int prerequisiteCount(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int course)

It must return the number of directed edges pointing at course (its in-degree).

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — course u must be taken before course v. Last line: the queried course.

Output Format:
One line with the number of direct prerequisites.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v, course < V

questions.title: Minimum Flight Hops
questions.description:
An airline's route map is an undirected graph where every leg costs one hop. The fewest hops between two cities is the BFS shortest distance. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int minHops(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int s, int t)

It must return the minimum number of edges on a path from s to t, or -1 when t is unreachable. Travelling from s to itself costs 0 hops.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a flight route. Last line: "s t" — origin and destination.

Output Format:
One line with the hop count, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= s, t, u, v < V

questions.title: Reachable Server Alert
questions.description:
A monitoring tool must raise an alert only if a compromised server can eventually reach a critical target through any chain of directed links. Reachability is a simple graph search. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int reachable(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g, int s, int t)

It must return 1 if t is reachable from s (following directed edges, any length, including the trivial path s -> s), otherwise 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a directed link. Last line: "s t" — source and target.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= s, t, u, v < V

questions.title: Build System Cycle Check
questions.description:
A build orchestrator resolves module dependencies; a directed cycle among modules would deadlock every build. Detect it with a DFS that colours nodes white (0, unvisited), grey (1, on the current stack) and black (2, finished): a cycle exists exactly when an edge reaches a grey node. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int hasCycle(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return 1 if the directed graph contains a cycle, otherwise 0. You may write additional static helpers.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a directed dependency u depends on v.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Network Partition Queries
questions.description:
After a data-centre reorganisation, racks were merged into zones by a sequence of undirected links. Operations then asks many questions of the form "are rack a and rack b in the same zone?" — the classic union-find workload: union all links once, then answer every query with two find calls. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static String[] connectivityQueries(int v, int[][] edges, int[][] queries)

It must process every link with union operations and return, for each query {a, b}, "YES" if a and b are connected, else "NO" (queries answered in order). You may write additional static helpers.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — an undirected link. Then a line Q. Then Q lines, each "a b" — a connectivity query.

Output Format:
Q lines, each YES or NO, in query order.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 1 <= Q <= 10, 0 <= a, b, u, v < V

questions.title: Ring Road Detection
questions.description:
City planners want to know whether the proposed road network contains a closed loop. In an undirected graph, a DFS that remembers the node it came from (the parent) finds a cycle exactly when it meets an already-visited node that is not its parent. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int hasUndirectedCycle(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return 1 if the undirected graph (no self-loops, no parallel edges) contains a cycle, otherwise 0. You may write additional static helpers.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — an undirected road.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Fiber Backbone Cost
questions.description:
A telecom operator must connect every exchange into one backbone at minimum total lease cost — the minimum spanning tree. Kruskal's greedy algorithm sorts the edges by weight and unions the cheap ones, skipping any edge whose endpoints are already connected. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int mstWeight(int v, int[][] edges)

Each row edges[i] = {u, v, w}. It must return the total weight of a minimum spanning tree (the graph is guaranteed connectable). You may write additional static helpers.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v w" — an edge between u and v with weight w.

Output Format:
One line with the MST total weight.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 1 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V, 1 <= w <= 1000

questions.title: Pipeline Longest Chain
questions.description:
A data pipeline is a DAG: each stage feeds later stages. Planning wants the longest dependency chain — the maximum number of stages that can run one after another. Processing stages in topological order and propagating a depth value solves it. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int longestChain(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

The input graph is guaranteed acyclic. It must return the largest number of nodes on any directed path (a single node counts as 1).

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — stage u feeds stage v (0-indexed, acyclic).

Output Format:
One line with the longest chain length in nodes.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Friend Circle Count
questions.description:
A social platform stores friendships as an undirected graph; a friend circle is a connected component. Counting the circles is a flood of BFS sweeps over unvisited nodes. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int componentCount(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return the number of connected components in the undirected graph (an isolated node counts as one circle). You may write additional static helpers.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — a friendship.

Output Format:
One line with the number of friend circles.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Course Schedule Order
questions.description:
Given prerequisites as a DAG, produce an order in which every course can be taken. Kahn's algorithm repeats: among ALL nodes currently having in-degree 0, always pick the SMALLEST index next, then delete its outgoing edges. That smallest-index tie-break makes the order unique. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] topoOrder(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

The input graph is guaranteed acyclic. It must return the topological order of all V nodes under the smallest-index tie-break.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — course u must be taken before course v (0-indexed, acyclic).

Output Format:
One line with the V node indices in the required order, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Emergency Response Distance
questions.description:
A dispatcher routes an ambulance from depot 0 through a road network to hospital n-1. Each road carries a travel-time weight; the matrix is symmetric and 0 means no road. Dijkstra's algorithm repeatedly settles the closest unsettled node and relaxes its edges. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int dijkstra(int[][] w)

w is the V x V weighted adjacency matrix. It must return the shortest travel time from node 0 to node n-1, or -1 when the hospital is unreachable.

Input Format:
Line 1: V. Then V lines, each with V space-separated integers — the weighted adjacency matrix (0 means no edge).

Output Format:
One line with the shortest distance from 0 to n-1, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= weight <= 1000

questions.title: Team Assignment Check
questions.description:
A workshop splits attendees into two teams so that every pair-project links people from DIFFERENT teams — possible exactly when the graph is bipartite, i.e. it contains no odd cycle. BFS 2-colouring decides it: give each node the opposite colour of its neighbour. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int isBipartite(ArrayList<ArrayList<Integer>> g)

It must return 1 if the undirected graph can be 2-coloured, otherwise 0. Isolated nodes are trivially colourable. You may write additional static helpers.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines, each "u v" — an undirected partnership.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 200, 0 <= u, v < V

questions.title: Island Count Survey
questions.description:
A satellite survey returns a character grid: '1' cells are land, '0' is water. An island is a maximal group of land cells connected horizontally or vertically (not diagonally). Flood fill from every unvisited land cell counts the islands. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int islandCount(char[][] grid)

It must return the number of islands in the grid using 4-directional connectivity. You may write additional static helpers.

Input Format:
Line 1: R C. Then R lines, each C characters ('0' water, '1' land).

Output Format:
One line with the number of islands.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 10
